title: Material Energy Conservation Workshop
description: A mystical workshop where a damaged helmet and a translucent plant share a finite pool of material energy. The user redistributes roughness, metalness, transmission, and emissive intensity between the two objects using coupled sliders, where increasing a property on one object decreases it on the other. An undo/redo system tracks all adjustments as the user tries to match a randomly generated target material configuration displayed as ghost previews.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load DamagedHelmet.glb on the left and DiffuseTransmissionPlant.glb on the right, both on a dark reflective ground plane. Use an environment map via RGBELoader (venetian_crossroads_1k.hdr from polyhaven or a neutral PMREMGenerator-created env). Camera at (0,1.5,4) looking at origin with OrbitControls.

Core mechanic: A conserved energy pool of 2.0 total units governs four material properties: roughness, metalness, emissive intensity, and transmission (opacity-inverse for the helmet). Each property has a coupled slider (HTML range input) that sets the helmet's value; the plant automatically receives (1.0 minus helmet's value) for that property. All four slider values must sum to exactly 2.0 across both objects (conservation law). When the user adjusts one slider, auto-clamp the last-edited other slider to maintain the sum constraint. Display the current sum prominently.

On load, generate a random target configuration (four values summing to 2.0) and render semi-transparent ghost duplicates of both models showing target materials at 30% opacity. Display a match percentage (0-100%) comparing current vs target using Euclidean distance.

Implement an undo/redo stack (arrays of state snapshots). Each slider change pushes state. Undo (Ctrl+Z or button) and Redo (Ctrl+Y or button) restore previous states and update all sliders and materials. Provide a 'New Target' button to randomize a new goal. Add a 'Reset' button restoring defaults.

Apply properties in real-time: traverse each model's meshes, set material.roughness, material.metalness, material.emissiveIntensity (with emissive color white), and material.transmission (enable material.transparent). Use MeshPhysicalMaterial features. Add two point lights (warm and cool) plus ambient light. Show a congratulatory message when match exceeds 95%. Style the UI panel with a semi-transparent dark overlay on the left side.
